questions.question: Who ascended the throne after the death of Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mohammad bin Tughlaq**__.

__
 
• Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq was succeeded by his son Mohammad Bin Tughlaq.
 
• Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq was the founder of the Tughlaq dynasty.
 
• He founded Tughlaqabad city and constructed the Tughlaqabad fort.
 
• He made reforms in the field of judiciary, irrigation, and agriculture.
 
• He died in 1325 by collapsing a building during a celebration of his victory.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** Mohammad Bin Tughlaq

• He is well known for his disastrous decision of transferring his capital from Delhi to Devagiri.
 
• Firoz Shah Tughlaq was the nephew of Mohammad Bin Tughlaq ruled from 1351 to 1388.
 
• Naseeruddin Mohammad Shah Tughlaq was the last ruler of Tughlaq dynasty .
 
• The Tughlaq Dynasty lasted from 1320 to 1414 AD.

questions.question: In India, a microfinance loan is defined as a collateral-free loan given to a household having an annual income of up to Rs _________ as of October 2022.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rs 3 lakhs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A loan without security issued to a household with an annual household income of up to 3,00,000 is referred to as a microfinance loan.
 
• The criterion for household income was standardized between rural and urban families under the new regulations, which went into effect on April 1, 2022, and the cap was raised to 300,000 rupees for all lenders, including banks, non-banking financial institutions, and stand-alone microlenders.
 
• A non-banking financial organization previously classified as a microfinance institution used a household income cap of 125,000 rupees for rural areas and 200,000 for urban and semi-urban areas to identify microfinance borrowers.
 
• The loan ceiling for private borrowers was established at 125,000 rupees.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Any guidelines, circulars, notifications, regulations, rules, or other restrictions, as well as any decisions or determinations relevant to taxes, common currency, financial stability standards, and other prudential standards on revenue recognition, asset valuation, and provisioning relative to disbursements by banks and financial institutions, liquidity, reserve requirements, reserve assets, special deposit cash ratios, capital asset requirements, or any other form of regulation, are referred to as RBI directions.

questions.question: Which of the following is the richest source of Vitamin C?
questions.solution:

__
 
• Lemons contain about 31 grams of Vitamin C.
 
• It is also known as ascorbic acid and is found in citrus fruits (like orange, and lemon), kiwifruit, guava, broccoli, strawberries, etc. 
 
• It is an essential nutrient and is not synthesized by the human body. It is a water-soluble vitamin.
 
• Functions - Repair of tissues, acts as a co-factor in many enzymatic reactions, important for the Immune system, acts as an antioxidant.
 
• C6H8O6 is the chemical formula of Vitamin C.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• It is on the List of Essential Medicines of the World Health Organization.
 
• Deficiency Disease - The deficiency of Vitamin C causes scurvy. 
 
• Discovery - It was discovered in 1912 and first isolated in 1928.

questions.question: What type of energy conversion takes place in a battery?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chemical energy into electrical energy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Chemical energy__ is converted into electrical energy by a battery.

 __
 
• A battery is a device that stores chemical energy and converts it to electrical energy.
 
• The chemical reactions in a battery involve the flow of electrons from one material (electrode) to another, through an external circuit.
 
• The flow of electrons provides an electric current that can be used to do work.
 
• To balance the flow of electrons, charged ions also flow through an electrolyte solution that is in contact with both electrodes.
 
• A battery can be made up of one or several electrochemical cells.
 
• The invention of the battery as we know it is credited to the Italian scientist Alessandro Volta.​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Energy Transformation
 Explanation
 Example
 
 
 
 

 Chemical Energy into Light Energy
 This transformation occurs when energy stored in chemical bonds is released as light energy.
 A glow stick is an example of this. The chemical reaction inside the glow stick releases energy in the form of light.
 
 

 Mechanical Energy into Chemical Energy
 This transformation occurs when mechanical energy, or work, is used to produce chemical energy.
 In photosynthesis, plants use the mechanical energy of photon particles (light) to transform carbon dioxide and water into glucose (chemical energy).
 
 

 Chemical Energy into Sound Energy
 This transformation occurs when energy stored in a substance is released in the form of sound.
 In fireworks, the chemical energy in the gunpowder is transformed into sound energy (the boom you hear), as well as light and heat energy.

• Lakshadweep islands are located in the Arabian sea. 
 
• As these islands are built up by corals, they are called as Coral Islands of India.
 
 
 
• **Dadra and Nagar Haveli****​**

questions.question: Megasthenes was a Greek ambassador in the court of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** ​Chandragupta Maurya**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chandragupta Maurya:**

 
 
• **Chandragupta Maurya** was the founder of the** Maurya Empire in ancient India**.
 
• He built one of the largest-ever empires on the **Indian subcontinent **and then, according to **Jain sources**, he renounced it all to become a **Jain monk**.
 
• **Megasthenes **served as an **ambassador of Seleucus I of Syria to the court of Chandragupta Maurya.**
 
• His observations were recorded in his work called **'Indica'.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pushyamitra Shunga:**

 
 
• He was a ruler of the **Shunga Empire in North India, after he overthrew the Maurya Empire**.
 
• **Pushyamitra Shunga** ruled for **36 years** and was succeeded by his son** Agnimitra**.
 
 
 
• **Harshvardhana**:
 
 
• Also known as **Harsha,** he was an I**ndian emperor who ruled North India from 606 to 647 CE.**
 
• He was the son of **Prabhakarvardhana **and the** younger brother of Rajyavardhana, a king of Thanesar, Haryana.**
 
• **Megasthenes **did not serve in **his court, as his time was much later than that of Megasthenes.**
 
 
 
• **Ashoka**:
 
 
• **Ashoka** was an** Indian emperor of the Maurya Dynasty who ruled almost all of the Indian subcontinent from c. 268 to 232 BCE.**
 
• One of **India's greatest emperors, Ashoka reigned over a realm that stretched from the Hindu Kush mountains in the west to Bengal in the East and covered the entire Indian subcontinent except parts of present-day Tamil Nadu and Kerala.**

questions.question: The Deccan Plateau is a triangular landmass in India that lies to the south of the river ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Narmada**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Narmada: **

 
 
• **The Narmada River flows through the states of Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat,** moving **westwards over a length of about 1,312 km before emptying into the Arabian Sea in the Bharuch district of Gujarat.**
 
• This river is considered the traditional boundary between** North India and South India, with the Deccan Plateau lying south** of it. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ganga:**

 
 
• **The Ganges or Ganga** is one of the **longest rivers in India,** and it flows through the **northern part of the country**.
 
• **The Deccan Plateau** is not located south of this river; instead,** it's geographically much further south**.
 
 
 
• **Krishna:**
 
 
• **The Krishna River** is one of the major rivers in **India, flowing through the states of Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh.**
 
• It does flow through t**he Deccan Plateau,** but it's not the river that traditionally marks the northern boundary of the plateau.
 
 
 
• **Tapi:**
 
 
• **The Tapi River (also known as Tapti)** runs in **central India between the Godavari and Narmada rivers.**
 
• It flows westwards over a **length of 724 km **before draining through the **Gulf of Khambhat into the Arabian Sea**.

• The Ramosi Peasant Force was an armed force formed by the Ramosi people of the Sahyadri mountain range in India in the late 1820s to revolt against the British East India Company.

questions.question: The ancient harvest festival of Baisakhi is celebrated in which month of the year?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**April**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Baisakhi,** also known as **Vaisakhi, is a historical and religious festival in Sikhism and Hinduism**.
 
• It is usually celebrated on **April 13 or 14 every year**, marking the Sikh new year.
 
• For Sikhs, it commemorates the formation of the Khalsa panth of warriors under Guru Gobind Singh Ji in 1699.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **November:** In India, several other festivals do occur in November, including **Diwali, the festival of lights, and Guru Nanak Jayanti, the birth anniversary of Guru Nanak, the founder of Sikhism.**
 
• **August:** In August, some of the notable Indian festivals include **Raksha Bandhan, which celebrates the bond between brothers and sisters, and Janmashtami, which marks the birth of Lord Krishna.**
 
• **January:** Makar Sankranti and Pongal, two major harvest festivals in India, are celebrated in this month, along with the national celebration of **Republic Day on January 26th.**

questions.question: Ramappa Temple is dedicated to which God?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Shiva**__.

• The** Ramappa Temple, **also known as the **Ramalingeswara Temple, is dedicated to Lord Shiva.**
 
• The temple is located in the village of **Palampet, Venkatapur Mandal, in the Mulugu district of the Indian state of Telangana.**
 
• The **Ramappa Temple** is a **remarkable example of Kakatiya architectural style, named after the sculptor Ramappa who built it, as per the instructions of the general Recherla Rudra during the Kakatiya rule in 1213 AD.**
 
• It's known for its** intricate carvings and exquisite sculpture, featuring themes from Hindu mythology, epic narratives, and folklore.**
 
• The temple's notable elements include its **sandstone sculptures, floating bricks, intricate carvings, and a dancing hall with unique pillars.**

questions.question: Mosses and lichens are found in which kind of forest?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Tundra Forest**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mosses and lichens** are most commonly found in the **Tundra Forest.**
 
• **Key reasons include:**__
 __
 
• **Cold Climate:** The tundra is characterized by **very cold temperatures**.
 
 
• Mosses and lichens can survive these** extreme conditions as they are adapted to cold climates.**
 
 
 
• **Short Growing Season: **The growing season in the **tundra is very short, but mosses and lichens can grow and reproduce quickly during this period.**
 
• **Low-Nutrient Soil: **The tundra has** low-nutrient soil, which is suitable for mosses and lichens, as they can grow on poor substrates.**
 
• **Limited Competition: **In the harsh conditions of the tundra, **there are fewer competing species, which allows mosses and lichens to thrive.**
 
• **Tolerance to Drought and Frost: **Mosses and lichens have a **high tolerance to drought and frost, which makes them suitable for the tundra environment.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.concept: Socio - Religious Reform Movements in the 19th and 20th CE India
questions.question: The ______ was started by the Sikh reformers to purify their religious places by removing the evil social practices that had slowly crept into them.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the Akali Movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Akali Movement was started in the early 20th century by Sikh reformers.**
 
• The primary aim was to liberate **Sikh gurdwaras from the control of corrupt priests who were influenced by British rule in India.**
 
• The movement sought to **remove social evils and restore the purity of religious practices that had slipped into the gurdwaras.**
 
• The movement led to the **Sikh Gurdwaras Act of 1925, which transferred the control of gurdwaras to the elected bodies of the Sikh community.**
 
• This movement played a crucial role in awakening the **masses and strengthening the spirit of freedom, which eventually contributed to the broader Indian independence movement.**
 
• The **Akali Movement not only focused on religious reform but also brought political and social change, leading to a greater sense of unity among Sikhs.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Movement
 Key Points
 
 
 
 

 Namdhari Movement
 
 
Started in the mid-19th century by Baba Ram Singh.

 
It was a socio-religious reform movement among the Sikhs and an early rebellion against British rule.

 
Namdharis are also known as "Kuka" because of their unique style of reciting the "Kirtan."

 
 
 

 Ghadar Movement
 
 
Formed in 1913 by Indian immigrants from the United States and Canada.

 
Its objective was to overthrow British colonial authority in India by means of an armed revolution.

 
Lala Hardayal, Sohan Singh Bhakna, and Bhagat Singh were among its key leaders.

 
 
 

 Nirankari Movement
 
 
Began in the early 19th century as a reform movement within Sikhism.

 
It emphasized the worship of God as Nirankar (formless), rejecting the belief in avatars.

 
The movement eventually separated from mainstream Sikhism and became an independent spiritual path.
